name: c3e8fe0add84
claim: Peer outbox delivery has no standalone flush script; the canonical entry point is the flush-outbox subcommand of lan_peer_assign.py (cmd_flush_outbox with its own argparse subparser), and every launcher or doc that flushes wraps that same subcommand, with remap and launcher behavior pinned by dedicated tests such as the flush-remap and start-sh peer-flush-control tests; prefer the documented subcommand over ad-hoc HTTP delivery scripts.

decisions.notes: A repo-wide filename search for flush scripts returned only tests; the implementation lives as cmd_flush_outbox behind the flush-outbox subparser of lan_peer_assign.py, and both platform launchers plus the skill docs invoke that subcommand.

rationale: One canonical subcommand keeps delivery semantics, trust checks and receipts in one audited code path; ad-hoc delivery scripts would bypass those gates.
